The summary is cautious, reaches an 'inconclusive' lean, flags the thin documentation, and the examples fit the cited claims. The weaknesses are a few small inaccuracies and some tension in the narrative.","problems":["The headline says the returned charts 'support the billed level', while the rationale says some supported notes look odd and that they are weak signs of inflated documentation. This is slightly inconsistent.","The claim that the excess 'shows up in every complexity stratum' is loosely true: the 5+ stratum is 0.25 vs 0.236, which is essentially no excess. The statement that it is 'sharpest among 0 or 1 conditions' is also wrong, because the 3-condition stratum has the highest share (0.345) and the 0-condition stratum has only 0.062.","The 'sharpest among 0 or 1 conditions' claim contradicts the by_complexity table, so the evidence for it is misread.","The cited examples in the code-written section include only one documentation example (C0056517, a 99214) and two low-complexity claims; the 99215 claims named in the rationale (C0056566, C0056672, C0056690, C0056698, C0056542) are not in cited_claim_ids.","The next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs are requested, although the rationale prioritises 99215 claims on patients with 0-1 conditions. 'Re-screen once records arrive' adds little.","C0056690 is described as 'follow-up Z09 only', an interpretation that goes beyond the card data."]}
